1、局外成长幅度低到可以忽略，经典的刷5W魂提升10点血量，而且成长不涉及伤害，前期3枪死的小兵后期还是3枪死。20级左右升一级大概就是2W魂左右，2图你舔完差不多也就2W5的魂，一张图舔完大概30分钟吧， 2、局内资源不随难度提升，灵视0的情况下加上地图两个弹药箱有溢出，灵视1的就频繁出现高强度战斗子弹得掐着用的情况了，灵视2打两场战斗就烧完了你的子弹，弹药箱还在地图深处给隔开了。同时近战、法术等还是杀敌回复，意思就是你没子弹了就是个纯废人，近战肘不出伤害（幽默无充能肘击打20，最基础小怪都有100血），法术没法充能 3、堆怪，堆高性能怪，二图开始堆火枪，三图开始堆榴弹怪，火枪子弹飞行速度快，只能提前预判闪避，榴弹平飞速度也不慢，然后还带爆炸伤害，更难躲，然后些B还都硬得一笔，火枪狙击打头3枪，榴弹更是7枪往上走，没法快速清理，对面重火力洗地，而你只是一个拎着大栓的猎巫人 4、巨大的营地活动范围：二图右边入口最容易体会到，出门就是两个营地中间，打下面的A营地B营地的人也过来了，有时候还会引到悬崖下面的C营地的榴弹兵，曲线火力在悬崖底下炸你悬崖顶上一点不带歪的。其他地方也经常出现打着打着突然告诉你营地清理完毕，然后场上还剩十万八千个怪。 5、巡逻队，配合上3+4，经常打着打着你背后就是一队巡逻给你夹了 6、幽默至极的衰减距离，SMG和左轮大概15米就能见到明细的伤害衰减，大概减50%，17米就直接衰减到1。不是哥们，这距离我用手丢石头都能丢过去，你左轮和SMG就只能打1血了，你这枪还不如弹弓呢。 7、幽默至极的专注系统，你在专注状态下，瞄准敌人然后闪避能看到敌人的弱点，然后打掉全部弱点敌人可以进入眩晕，眩晕状态下受到伤害增加。很强是吧，又有控制又有增伤，那么，怎么才能进入专注状态呢，那就是耐力全满，听上去很简单对不对，但是这SB游戏挨打扣你耐力上限，玻璃人挨一下就掉耐力上限了，耐力上限掉了就回不满耐力了捏。耐力上限又只能靠杀敌回复。纯纯的优势用不上劣势没得用的玩意儿。 8、魂掉落位置又是不动脑子的留原地，经典的我不清图没有局内成长不好打BOSS，打完局内成长去打BOSS没打过我魂全掉里面了。魂好歹还给你个返回骨片呢 9、傻逼解密，硬藏，灵视2之后解锁一个看门人的路障机制，把地图要道直接给你拦住，提示你要找一前一后两个能量源。范围不给你圈，视觉听觉提示啥都没有，要不是我运气好找到了一个我都不知道这玩意儿长啥样，只有一个小巫火块大的东西，随机刷在一个石头缝里面。至于另一个能量源，对不起找不到。 战斗概括：主角整体防御性能极低，攻击性能方面又缺乏快速清版手段，只能打打顺风仗，一旦陷入劣势局面只有一手重型法术能救一波，一旦重型法术救场失败，就可以摆了。 肝度概括：30分钟清图还有概率翻车，清完图不一定能升一级，升一级用处堪比蚊子腿，就硬刷，建议每个难度体验一下之后开叮跳过刷魂环节

Gnosis 2 之后，是真的没有一点游戏体验了。可能是我FPS菜吧，拿着强化满级的装备，城堡和Scarlet coast一直死，一直死，精英怪的区域一刷刷4个火炮手加两个天上飞的；打算把怪引出来一个一个解决呢，传送门又刷追兵了：四面夹击。 菜就算了，受伤多了还有Calamity等着我，要一边处理怪群一边预判飞船炸弹的飞行轨迹。Gnosis 1 之前我都把Calamity当作补充血瓶用的。现在真的是，清一个区域就能叫出一次Calamity…… 游戏性和很多创新点我都蛮喜欢的，但这个难度，恐怕不太适合我…… 压死骆驼的最后一根稻草是我拿着60K魂，打算试一下Scarlet Coast的boss，然后被一脚踩飞了。重新进地图发现魂在boss战场地，要过去的话又要先把全图清一遍。 对不起，我真的不喜欢被一群怪围着打。

刚刚打完第三章图的宝珠准备撤离，结果桥上的撤离点直接刷了一桥的怪，直接把剩下几秒解锁的撤离点干成一分钟，本身第三张图就是最卡的，这下电脑瞬间卡爆被怪围殴死。 凭空刷怪是个大问题，我对这游戏所有的负面印象大多都来自于这一机制。 不是说不能这么刷，本来也没必要一开始就把全图的怪刷出来，玩家电脑也吃不消；但是你tm不能在5s内在玩家方圆10米内刷20几只啊（不过这次短时间刷那么多确实罕见，之前没见过，怀疑是bug）；配上沟槽的耐力系统（挨打掉耐力→没耐力跑不快→跑不快继续挨打），玩家一旦短时间身边刷了大量的怪基本上可以准备开下一把了。 [h1] 刷怪刷远一点啊 [/h1] [b] 再说说这第三张图，可以说是除了依旧不错的美术以外完全是答辩 [/b] [list] [*]首先，有黑魂篝火彩蛋的出生点就极其逆天，一落地就会拉到怪物仇恨，那个位置附近还有地图三巨头之一；结果经常就是一落地在没有buff的情况下就开始恶战，大量小怪、精英怪、墙上挂着的喷毒面具还混杂着一个小boss，这个开局比这张图蜘蛛洞里的准boss还难打；跑也跑不掉，这个游戏的怪有超远的仇恨距离。 [*]还有沟槽的三巨头，全是普通小怪的加强版，要说设计也没什么设计，就是堆了数值；但是！他们会在上百米外突然感应到玩家，然后横跨几条街来追杀你，并且血量没比准boss差多少。也就是说除非你本来就打算打这三巨头，不然就得时时刻刻注意他们的位置；不然等小地图上出现两个或者三个骷髅头的时候，我建议直接去下水道打准boss撤离。但是这三巨头除了第一次击杀掉落的钥匙以外，完全没有打的价值，掉落物很一般。 [*]这张图卡是真的卡，其他的图帧数的都相当稳定，就这张图经常打着打着暴跌30帧。 [*]这张图的金库（山顶的别墅）也是答辩，没有任何引导，进去几个拉杆拉半天找不到路，撞到挂着的骨头还会在身后非常近的位置刷出精英怪来干你。找半天才知道要去捡钥匙而不是拉这堆B拉杆；打到最后一个房间，看到拉杆还以为是出路，结果直接被喷了一脸的火。刚才才告诉玩家栏杆是开门的，结果拐几个弯拉杆就变成喷火了？这tm是人想的出来的？弱引导的见多了，反向引导的游戏还是让人大开眼界，引导这块这游戏和隔壁红色沙漠一桌。 [/list] 吐槽是吐槽完了，既然都开始写了，那就正式地评一下这个游戏当前的版本。 优点就不说了，你看这游戏的好评率就知道它底子相当扎实,主要谈谈缺点. [h3] 引导太烂了 [/h3] 这个游戏的引导说好听点就是比游戏界的传奇Minecraft要优秀，毕竟它至少有引导；但是那个引导根本不足以支撑玩家的游玩，玩家依然需要大量的试错和事后总结才能搞清楚游戏的各种设定。 举个例子，那个会爆炸的脑袋。玩家第一次接到任务大多是一头雾水，根本不知道脑袋从何找起，只能随缘；但实际上，小地图会用一个几乎看不见的感叹号表面脑袋的位置——但是问题也出在这，这游戏除了任务道具还有其他东西会用这个感叹号来标记，玩家注意到感叹号时也不一定会把它和脑袋关联起来。好吧，就当玩家注意到接取任务的一瞬间注意到那个几乎看不见的感叹号了；当玩家找到那个脑袋，把它捡起来赶回去交任务的时候，路上“嘭”脑袋炸啦。之前没有任何提醒告知玩家这个脑袋会炸，更主要的是，玩家这时候并不明白脑袋为什么会炸：是遇到敌人了？是因为自己跑了？是因为任务超时了？是自己捡起来的方式不对？是因为自己缺少了前置道具？我在网上搜攻略的时候发现了玩家们在面对脑袋炸了之后不同的反应：蹲着送脑袋、滑铲送脑袋、跳着送脑袋……当然还有送个锤子，不送了。没有引导，玩家失误了却不明白为何失误，这可以说是极其糟糕；更逆天的是，像这么糟糕的设计还不止一个。 [h3] 撤不了 [/h3] 先说说撤离点种类，初始开局后几分钟内关闭的出生撤离点、局内一直存在的永久撤离点、击杀boss生成的撤离点。| 第一个出生撤离点基本上用不到，除非天崩开局（比如第三张图落地就被群怪+小boss围殴），不然那几分钟基本搜不到什么东西。 boss撤离点用的次数也不多，主要一般情况下没有打boss的必要，但是这个撤离点的好处就是不会消失也不用读条充能。 接下来就是重量级的永久撤离点，到达后需要读条二三十秒。其实光是这点也还好，也没什么搜达撤能在撤离点秒撤的。但是由于牵扯到另一个系统，情况就变得复杂起来了。这个撤离点还承担提供弹药的作用，以撤离点为中心会刷出携带弹药的小怪，因为玩家携带的初始弹药并不多，局内补充是相当有必要。但是这个设计和撤离点结合就让事情变得微妙起来，有可能你正在等待撤离点读条，结果小怪一刷，直接读条时间翻几倍。甚至有时候你在被小boss追杀的时候跑到了撤离点，眼看着要撤了，结果小怪一刷，直接拖到小boss赶到。这么一看，这个系统在没有小boss的图似乎还行，但是这些小怪提供的弹药非常少，你可能三枪打死一个然后给你补四发。这个系统在正反馈微乎其微的情况下，一旦触发负反馈甚至可能直接导致撤不走。 [h3] 模糊的边界 [/h3] 这个游戏的边界很模糊，比如屋顶，有的屋顶可以稳稳的站上去，有的会滑下来，有的干脆放空气墙不然上，玩家根本不知道能上还是不能上。有些地方也搞不清楚是能去还是开发者的疏忽所以可以过去的。 [h3] 凭空刷怪 [/h3] 好好说说这个沟槽的刷怪机制，也是我认为目前最大的败笔。 [list] [*]玩家一进地图，首先会根据据点生成零星的小怪和一些小boss，一旦玩家与小怪接战，据点就会开始大量刷怪。什么提前规划、什么逐个击破不存在的，全靠临场反应，这对玩家的快速反应要求非常高，有的怪会长距离位移、有的会自爆、有的会大老远开狙、有的会开盾、有的会打控制……所以打的时候不能看见啥打啥，要做好规划，但是这些凭空刷出来的怪又注定不会给你足够的时间思考。 [*]其次就是传送门刷怪，那点弹药我说真的你不如别刷；这些怪不像据点怪，他们可以跑到地图的各个地方，参杂在混战中；如果在混战中你打它马了几枪甚至还是倒贴弹药，自己提前买弹药包和地图的弹药箱才是有效补充手段。 [*]还有裂隙刷怪，这个算好的了，很多时候就刷那么两个，而且只有非常近的时候才会触发。 [*]挑战箱刷怪也是重量级，比如那个逐个击破，刷一堆怪但是每次只有一个怪会受伤，这就导致有时候几个近战打怪疯狂突脸你还打不了，你得去追杀那个躲在后方的远程怪；杀完一个怪后剩下哪一个怪解除了护盾你也得重新找。还有决斗挑战箱，给你一个不大的场地刷一个近战突脸怪，如果有控制法术或者带了近距离爆发武器还能打，要是拿着手枪和大狙还是离开范围解除挑战吧（或者干脆不开） [/list] 目前看来核心问题还是在于这个刷怪，玩家对情况没有具体的预期，甚至常常出现不知道怪哪冒出来。怪多、怪数值高是小事，但是被不知道哪冒出来的怪打死就很糟糕了。

Thoughts after 40 hours of playing Witchfire 1-The game’s visuals and gunplay feel absolutely fantastic. 2-Aside from its graphics and shooting feel, there is virtually nothing praiseworthy about it. 3-Enemies are endlessly spammed at you, yet you never get access to overpowered spells or high-impact firearms to counter this horde spam—turning constant monster waves into a major flaw. 4-The endless hordes are bad enough, but enemy AI is deliberately designed to frustrate players to no end. Foes dodge endlessly the moment you aim at them, even when you’re shooting straight at their backs like they have eyes on the back of their heads. Certain boss monsters and elite pursuers can lock onto and hit you perfectly from absurdly far distances. Without a long-range sniper rifle, you barely stand a chance to fight back. 5-The punitive mechanics make no sense at all. Once your corruption meter maxes out, an aerial dreadnought will sometimes spawn. If you didn’t bring a sniper, you’re basically left with no way to survive. 6-The game tries to cram every genre trope into itself and ends up satisfying no one. Horde combat and roguelite elements are meant to deliver satisfying, adrenaline-fueled slaughter, yet the game provides almost no health restoration on kills. Damage taken hits as harshly as a Souls-like title, but it lacks well-crafted elites, memorable bosses, and polished dodge/attack counterplay systems. Simply making enemies obnoxious does not make a proper Souls-style experience. 7-To reiterate: the game bombards you with constant negative feedback. Enemies bait your attention forward only to ambush you from behind in swarms; traps litter every inch of the map; teleporting turrets hound you; tiny spiders that do not appear on the minimap lurk everywhere. I cannot fathom why the developers chose to design the game purely to torment players. These annoyances might be tolerable for a slow-paced exploratory ARPG, but this is a repeat-run roguelite—no one wants to be punished over and over again during every grind session. My final verdict remains unchanged: stunning visuals and satisfying gunplay, but abysmal level design and infuriating enemy AI. Do not buy this game unless you enjoy being deliberately punished. The developers need to figure out their core design goal once and for all—do they want players to have fun, or do they want players to feel miserable? “巫火游戏时间40小时之后的感受 1-游戏的画面和枪械手感都很出色。 2-除了画面和枪械手感基本没有什么出色地方。 3-无脑堆怪但是不给与玩家更加强大的魔法或者更加夸张的枪械结果，这个堆怪变成了缺点。 4-无脑堆怪也算了，怪物的AI逻辑极度恶心玩家，玩家瞄准怪物就无限闪躲，而且我从怪物背后瞄准一样会闪躲。背后长眼睛一样。部分boss怪物或者特种追兵可以在900公里外瞄准而且精准命中玩家。而玩家如果不带远距离的狙击枪就基本没有反击方法。 5-不知所谓的惩罚机制，满诅咒后有时候刷一台“空中航母”。如果没带远距离狙击枪那么玩家只能等死。 6-游戏的定位明显是什么都想要，但什么都不讨好。堆怪和肉鸽这两种元素加起来就是为了玩家无脑刷刷刷释放肾上腺素，但是偏偏又没有很多击杀回复手段。而且血量扣除跟魂类游戏一样。如果想走魂游路线又没有出色的精英怪和boss设计和攻防闪避的逻辑。（不是把怪物设计得恶心就是魂游）。 7-还是那句话，负面反馈太多。什么前面的怪物勾引玩家视线然后从后面就几个怪物偷袭。什么满地都是陷阱。什么会瞬移的炮台。甚至是在小地图上不显示的小蜘蛛。完全不知道游戏设计师是为什么要这样恶心玩家。如果是ARPG慢慢探索的话可以忍，但这是一款反复刷的肉鸽游戏，谁会想被游戏反复折磨？ 我的总结没变，游戏画面和射击玩法都出色，但是关设计和怪物AI都很恶心。除非你是有受虐倾向，不然别买。游戏设计师应该要想明白这个游戏的核心是什么到底是想玩家爽还是想玩家恶心。” =============================================== Objective Review of Witchfire First off, the core mechanics and gameplay loop of this game are solid, yet wildly unfinished. I’ve beaten countless soulslikes: Dark Souls 3, Bloodborne, Remnant 2, and Space Marine 2. None of them flood the player with hordes of foes right out the gate. Instead, they let you gradually upgrade your gear while enemy encounters scale alongside your progress. Witchfire’s enemy scaling design, however, strikes me as utterly baffling. Enemies get absurdly tough before you’ve had a chance to grow stronger or even learn the game’s systems. Spamming endless swarms of monsters is bad enough, but foes also spawn out of thin air all around you. I’ll spot a handful of enemies ahead, only for more to materialize directly behind me. Is this design choice supposed to be fun? The soul retrieval mechanic works for traditional ARPGs, but this is a roguelite RPG. Enemy layouts are procedurally generated every run, with mobs spawning on all sides. It’s nearly impossible to recover your lost souls after dying. The rewards for exploration are nowhere near worth the risks; the game delivers far more negative feedback than positive. For a shooter, enemies boast far superior mobility and aim accuracy than the player character. There are almost no viable counterplay options when swarmed by dozens of foes. If you’re going to throw melee-focused elite enemies at players, at the very least add a block mechanic. Players are forced to leap and dart around like monkeys, frantically firing while dodging bullets and melee strikes nonstop. Take inspiration from Space Marine 2. The difficulty here is already comparable to Space Marine 2’s Brutal Plus mode. At this stage, I genuinely cannot recommend purchasing this game. “关于这款游戏的《Witchfire》客观评价 首先游戏的底层逻辑和玩法是好的，但完全不完善。 我通关很多魂类游戏《黑暗之魂3》《血源诅咒》《遗迹2》《星际战士2》 都不是一开始就堆怪，而是一步步慢慢加强装备同时加强敌人配置。 但是《Witchfire》的敌人加强配置真的让我匪夷所思。 玩家没有变强也没有熟悉游戏时敌人配置就强的离谱。 无脑堆怪就算了，怪物还凭空刷新这我四周。 我前面看到几个怪物身后就凭空刷新几个。这种设计很好玩吗？ 角色死亡要捡魂这个设计在ARPG游戏里面成立，但你这是一款带有肉鸽属性的RPG游戏。 每次敌人配置都随机生成，而且四周围生成。基本很难去吧之前丢的魂捡回来。 探索的回报和风险根本不成正比，负面反馈比正面反馈大太多。 作为一款设计游戏敌人的灵活性和射击准度远高于玩家。 玩家面对成群的敌人根本没有什么好的对应手段。 既然有近战强化敌人，你至少给玩家一个格挡吧？ 玩家被迫跟个猴子一样，一边射击一边上蹿下跳躲子弹躲近战。 你们参考一下《星际战士2》吧。你这么这个游戏的难度都比得上《星际战士2》的残酷+难度了。 目前为止我真的不建议购买这款游戏。”

An incredible surprise; I can't stop playing Witchfire. You'll see Witchfire tagged as an "Extraction Shooter" and I don't think that's quite accurate. The only thing you're "extracting" is currency. It doesn't have a loop similar to Tarkov, Marathon, Arc Raiders, etc. Instead, Witchfire really is something closer to Warframe or Destiny, stripped of the live-service elements and made single-player. There's no loot per se. You have a relatively small arsenal of weapons, spells, and accessories, all of which you grind out to unlock increasingly powerful, meaningful, and gameplay-altering upgrades. The game keeps pace with your ever-increasing power by continuously introducing new twists and wrinkles. New enemies on old maps, new traps, new events, etc. It looks great, sounds great, and runs great. It's pleasantly repetitive with enough nuance and long-term progression to keep it engaging.

Good atmosphere with grim lore, decent graphics and artstyle. Pleasant gunplay. Large detailed shelter that can be upgraded and used to research weapons, buffs and perks. Structured story and progression system. Overall good basis for a great game. So what is wrong with the game at the moment? First of all - repetetiveness and grind amount. Maps are small for extration shooter game, they quickly became boring and it is hard to evade complex attacks of enemy hordes in small areas. No stealth options. You literally just need to kill-grind same small areas again and again to progress. Weapons deal 1 point of damage if enemy is not in close range (it is valid even for long barrel rifles that shoot effectively only like 20-30 m). Maps almost does not change between runs. If you die twice in a row without extraction - those 2 runs progress and loot is gone. Every character level requires more and more grind exponentially. You are not welcome here - this phrase from the trailer describes game perfectly. Difficulty can not be changed and it is not balanced. Game can spawn enemies just behind you and every their attack is very painful. Healing potions and ammo crates are rare. Some bosses are overpowered insanely. In your first TUTORIAL mission you can meet the first boss that can kill you in single hit. To summon the second in-game big boss you need to clear all map locations just in order to die in a minute from first attack that is AOE and penetrates all cover. Dungeouns are even better - kill everything that game spawns on you in small spaces where evasion can be deadly for you (because you will fall and die) while timer is ticking. Try it only if you are Dark Souls and Hunt fan that want some intense and tryhard PvE action. May be I will return to this game later, but for now it is a rage quit.

看了最新的开发者日志还是非常期待的，能认真听玩家意见的游戏不多，更不用说游戏现阶段的品质已经非常高了。不过个人还是有几个建议： 我认为在审判阵亡猎巫人后保留他们的灵魂比较好（或者至少以其他形式让他们可以被召唤），而非直接消失。大多数玩家都对剧情抱有好奇心，想探究七位猎巫人各自的故事结局，因此通关审判本就是几乎所有玩家都会推进的内容。但目前审判结束后对应猎巫人会直接退场，让玩家损失了应对棘手情况的核心手段（比如天灾降临时的疯狂侵蚀）。审判后留下的念珠也不足以弥补缺失的功能（念珠的栏位太有限竞争很激烈）。同时也让回声这种货币大幅失去作用，破坏了原有收集回声召唤、强化猎巫人的循环。此外七位猎巫人全部消散后，整个隐修所会变得空旷冷清，毫无生机。隐修所也是玩家休整、歇息的据点，空荡荡的环境会削弱据点的氛围感与归属感。 灵知提升后，游戏的难度的提升很大程度上不是依赖简单堆高怪物数值来实现的，而是在地图中增加更多机制、事件和抉择，这点非常非常难得。不过也要检查下一些事件的风险和收益的比例，有些事件体感上有点得不偿失。还有堆怪不要太狠了，跳脸刷怪的机制也一定要克制使用（最好给玩家一点提示和反应空间）。毕竟这游戏挨打会掉体力，没体力就会继续挨打，忽然被怪包围持续连死挫败感有点强的。 After reading the latest dev log, I’m really excited about the game’s future. There aren’t many developers who listen carefully to player feedback, and on top of that, the game already boasts outstanding quality at this stage of Early Access. I have a few suggestions to put forward: I hope the souls of fallen witch-hunters remain summonable after finishing their Trials, or at the very least add an alternative way to call them, instead of making them disappear permanently. Most players are curious about the lore and want to uncover the full endings of all seven witch-hunters, so clearing each Trial is content almost everyone will complete. Right now, however, finishing a Trial removes that witch-hunter entirely, robbing players of a key tool to deal with tough threats such as Madness corruption during Omens. The rosary beads rewarded after Trials cannot make up for this loss of functionality. Rosary slots are far too limited, forcing tough trade-offs between different useful beads. This change also devalues Echoes significantly and breaks the core loop of collecting Echoes to summon and upgrade witch-hunters. What’s more, once all seven hunters fade away, the Hermitorium becomes empty and lifeless. The Hermitorium acts as our hub for rest and recovery, so this hollow atmosphere weakens immersion and our sense of attachment to the base. I really admire how difficulty scales with higher Gnosis levels. Rather than mindlessly inflating enemy stats to raise challenge, the game adds more environmental mechanics, world events and meaningful choices across maps — this design approach is rare and excellent. That said, the risk-reward balance of several events needs reworking; many of them feel not worthwhile given the dangers involved. Also, please ease up on massive mob swarms and restrain sudden point-blank enemy spawns. It would be great to add advance warnings so players have time to react. Taking hits drains stamina in Witchfire, and with zero stamina you get stuck in a stagger loop and keep taking constant damage. Getting suddenly surrounded and chained to death out of nowhere creates a great deal of unnecessary frustration.

I mean, the game is really not for me; my perception is that it has souls-like DNA to it, and I do not really like those. On the first few difficulties, I did have a lot of fun. Some people say that playing the maps over and over again gets boring, but I disagree; when the game has a difficulty curve (and it also adds new stuff to the map with every [b]GNOSIS[/b]), it does feel good to master it. However, assuming that a normal person would up the [b]GNOSIS[/b] level the moment they can, like in any other video game with the perception of constant progression, the difficulty will get ridiculous very fast. After a while, I just accepted I won't be able to see all the stuff that can be unlocked with a higher GNOSIS, because I really do not want it to get even harder when I can barely get out without getting pummeled once, and if I die twice, I lose everything. When you upgrade the character, the character's power level does not pace well with the difficulty of the maps themselves. The map will cluster four areas together. When you start to shoot, you realize one of the areas is high-difficulty, and then it will start to spawn enemies around you. Then it will throw a second wave because one of the other areas is the highest-level difficulty. Then you kill those, and a horde of enemies that came out of the portal shows up. In the middle of it, one of the familiars (mini-bosses?) will appear and start shooting, and then while you are trying to manage it, you get swooped into another area, and then, and then... You end up fighting the whole map, which obviously means you will die before all the listed things happen, and there is not really a way to manage it at all. What ends up happening is you are constantly managing risk and extracting at the first chance, which means you just [i]grind[/i]. And the grind is the [b]worst[/b].

This game actually slaps. I went into Witchfire blind after seeing some of its artwork and environmental design, and BOY did it deliver. The atmosphere in this game is actually peak, and the sound design actually creates this tension that feels like it can be cut with a knife. The monster designs and the newly implemented lore is worthy of a tangent, but definitely not on here. Oh boy. I don't typically play single players since they don't really hold my attention, but this game has had me in a full stranglehold for the last two months. I had expectations, but I wasn't expecting anything like this. The genre seems to be a blend between roguelike and extraction, something that I haven't experienced before. The gunplay is on par with Destiny 2, the movement system feels incredible, and even the grind feels satisfactory. What makes this game feel so different from other roguelikes for me is the tension and the weight of each expedition. Losing a run in Gunfire Reborn or Risk of Rain 2 just feels like more of a time sink, but in Witchfire? You lose everything and can't get it back until you find your Corpse. I've never had to 'tactically retreat' before in any extraction shooter because it just never felt like I needed to. If you like high-stakes combat, and high-risk-high-reward style games, just buy it. Originally, I borrowed this from a friend's library and decided I loved it enough to buy it for myself. You won't regret it. It's one of the best early access games on Steam. Game's incredible and I'm looking forward to the updates in the future. My next tattoo will be one of the Arcana symbols.

I want to like this game, it has such a cool atmosphere to everything. The maps are detailed and feel lived in, the weapons have a really nice "medieval tech" feel to them, the lore and items all have a brutal appeal to them that's reminiscent of Warhammer. What is making me give this game a negative review is how punishing it is. Getting hit in this game drains your health obviously, but also drains stamina, reduces the max stamina (until you get focus back), removes perfect focus (which allows you to hit enemies hidden weak spots to stun them), slows you down briefly, and can raise the calamity gauge. One or two minor hits can easily snowball into a quick end to your run. Couple that with certain enemies that have very hard to dodge attacks and you quickly drift from "Tough but fair" to "annoying and frustrating". When it came to Dark Souls I always felt like I learned something from the death. "Ok, don't stand there when he raises his left arm slightly above his waist, don't dodge twice in a row during his combo without a brief pause, kite these enemies one by one", but with this game I don't feel like I learn anything. It's usually something like "two randoms from the portal jumped me while I was dealing with a boss and now I've taken three direct hits from him, end of run". As if to place an Eye Roll of a cherry on top of the This is Annoying cake there is the "git gud" crowd who come out of the wood works to say "Just run around and don't get hit." "I never had this problem."

Impressions in progress This game clearly has a vision. A vision thats inventive, full of meaningful progression mechanics and difficulty. Every single weapon has some sort of a substantial gimmick that you can also buildcraft around. An auto gun that heats up and deals higher damage when heated halfway thru while also dealing Burn status (but lower damage) and having faster reload speed when OVERheated. A revolver that powers up your bullets on reload for every critical hit you get before said reload. A machinegun pistol that regens your stamina and spells on kill, faster. A shotgun that recharges the magazine on special attack melee kills... and theres way more. Actually the only weapon i unlocked all the powers of so far is the first one mentioned above so i know the most about it. The rest have powers that are yet hidden to me so i only know their less upgraded form. And upgrading these weapons requires u to kill stuff with them and do their specific weapon actions tied to their gimmicks. And... then u have the spells. And relics. And rings. And fetishes. And demonic weapons. All these things oftentimes (always?) have some sort of interesting abilities that are often simple to understand/simple in concept and they are very cool. Like one relic that makes u discharge lightning after landing multiple shots. I combined that with a ring that makes me deal fire damage for a short while after a dash and then used that Heat weapon and another one that fires fast too (to trigger the relic ability) so now i deal both electric and fire damage and its badass. The itemization is pretty deterministic and theres no numbers/stat bloat, effects are pretty simple to understand. Theres also rougelike-like upgrades during runs, they further enchance u and have some fun things. But you still have a LOT of preset power when u plan out ur loadout, random upgrades during the runs are not the only major source of power. Your build "pre run" matters a lot and that is not affected by the randomnes. The game throws you out on "expeditions" which are somewhat similar to raids from Arc Raiders or Escape from Tarkov but its all singleplayer. Theres no definite timer per se but there are enemies that spawn over time from a portal and they will hunt you down. So its not as strict as having a raid fail just cuz of a time out but theres still a degree of war of attrition happening. And it can get really stressful when a portal raid party arrives when you are in a middle of another fight. Its hectic. The setting of the game is unique, Vatican forces hunting witches. The occult and supernatural atmosphere is brilliantly woven into gameplay. The game executes the idea that Bloodborne had with Insight but way better. Here, the inhuman-cosmic knowledge advances all the games mechanics and gives you a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of unlocks and makes the game harder and harder. Its a really exciting ramp up of unlocking new features and seeing crazy ♥♥♥♥ happen. The game starts out pretty simple, the maps are somewhat barren in comparison to playing on higher Gnosis (= Insight) levels. When u progress u start seeing new enemies, new world events... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ madness orbs are flying everywhere, some mad men are chanting in the corners, cursed chests appear, new kinds of portals appear, walls dissapear... theres more and more. The enemy design is engaging. So far most/all of the enemies have some sort of counter to them, it often comes down to dashing at the right moment but the way you dodge feels distinct enough between enemies. some enemies will shoot straight at you with long wind ups, others will bombard you, jump at u to melee, try to swarm u with their low hp but big numbers, do a series of teleports which u r supposed to dodge in their rhythm, throw madness orbs into the air which u will have to dispatch or avoid, otherwise u will go insane... many of these are pretty basic ideas but they are just executed well and comboed interestingly. they make for an engaging combat puzzle where u also have to figure out the priority of who to take on first. the combat pace at times feels a bit like Halo actually with the double jump feel but theres also the aftermentioned dodges which are very useful. Some of the more dangerous enemy types feel hard to learn though cuz it might take time to get to them and then u get killed fast and that can feel bad cuz u didnt even have a chance to learn and then u have to encounter them again to even have a chance at improvement. This makes me unsure if everything is actually balanced well cuz its hard to learn some of these enemies/situations. A big chunk is definitely balnced though. Theres some things that can be seen as questionable, like the timer in dungeons, so far its a very lenient though. edit: the timer seems to just give the optional rewards, thats even better. The calamity mechanic, which spawns some rather hard enemies and generally says "fuxk you" is stressful. Its also interesting. Not sure if good or bad, interesting. Need to play more to maybe get more pissed at it, idk. The difficulty overall ramps up constantly and its addicting and interestingly balanced, u see some new crazy BS and are like "there is no way im beating that" but then u try and actually find ways to overcome these obstacles and it works so well. Now i unlocked a new zone that seems even crazier than anything before and idk if it will happen again or i will actually constantly eat dirt lol. we will see. either way, u have ways to attain more power An unique game thats really worth a look. This is easily the best first person shooter ever made for me. The atmosphere is incredible. Graphics, design, sound. Everything is 100% on point. Looks absolutely stunning, sound design is INCREDIBLE. Runs flawlessly. ~300 FPS at 3440 x 1440 everything maxed, with framegen and DLSS quality on a 5080 + 3XD 9850. Had a couple of crashes, but the game is still in "early access". Gameplay is tense and really really strong. The progression system is very well designed. Each map becomes harder, as you level up the "Gnosis" difficulty level. Meanwhile Gnosis also adds new mechanics. There are a TON of mechanics, but not overwhelming, as each new mechanic gets introduced once at a time. Each map has a certain overall difficulty level, so it is always possible to jump back to an earlier map to farm Witchfire, to level the character. The risk/reward system works very well. You start a map, take a look at the setup, decide what to do in which order and while you progress, you constantly decide, if you have enough resources to push further or if you should go for a way to extract. There are several things to keep an eye on, like the escalation level, which at some point will start a stressful, dangerous event, ammo, health, healing items and so on. Guns! Guns are insanely well designed. Each gun has traits, that unlock by using it. Traits make the guns very unique! They all play differently and they all are balanced and have their situations, where they come in handy. Flat, big maps, with ranged enemies, require guns that focuse on precision, smaller, tighter maps require guns with focus on close combat. The guns and weapon traits remind me of Titanfall, because Titanfall only had a good selection of guns, but each was very different and had its on playstyle. And they all sound and feel incredible. Punchy bolt action rifle, powerful sniper, blasting shotguns, rattling machineguns. Just perfect! The spells and the buffs/debuffs are also great. Freeze enemies to blast at them, burn them to increase damage, shock them to do damage to multiple foes. Just perfect. Character builds are very versatile. Lots of options, lots of possible playstyles. As you progess a map, you become stronger and stronger, until you are a rolling death-machine. I absoluelty 100% recommend this game to anyone, who likes atmosphere-rich first person shooters, with a certain seriousness in regards to difficulty. This game is a pure joy to play and I hope this game succeeds just as hard as Dark Souls, Doom or anything alike. Hats of to the devs for creation a 10/10 masterpiece!
